summary: Backend-only verification of iteration 31: new GSMArena-backed spec-template endpoint GET /api/products/master/91mobiles-specs. Wrote pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_iteration31_91mobiles_specs.py — 19 tests across 6 classes covering auth (401/422), payload shape, category coverage (all 11 tabs), specs-filled threshold (>=50), real-value asserts (iPhone 15 Screen Size contains '6.1', Launch Date contains '2023'), Mongo cache hit (<1500ms round-trip), 5 popular phones (iPhone 15, Galaxy S24 Ultra, OnePlus 12R, POCO X6 Pro, Pixel 8), graceful 404s (unknown brand + unmatchable name), regression checks for /api/products/master/search and /api/products, and vendor create-with-IMEI persistence. ALL 19 TESTS PASS (100%). Live cold-fetch works (GSMArena returned 200 for every brand catalog and detail page). iPhone 15 payload: specs_filled=65/73, Screen Size='6.1 inches', Launch Date='2023, September 12', Chipset='Apple A16 Bionic (4 nm)'. Cache hit round-trip ~400-800ms (Mongo lookup + preview network). One QUALITY issue found (not blocking): fuzzy matcher picks 'Poco X6 Neo' when asked for 'POCO X6 Pro' — the actual POCO X6 Pro exists on GSMArena but the score of the Neo variant beats it in _pick_best_match because 'pro' vs 'neo' aren't disambiguated strongly enough (both are 3-letter non-numeric tokens). specs_filled still hits 65/73 so the test passes, but the returned matched_name is a semantically wrong device.

minor.issue: Fuzzy matcher returns matched_name='Poco X6 Neo' instead of the actual 'Poco X6 Pro'. Both share {poco, x6} tokens; 'pro'/'neo' aren't given decisive weight, so overlap 2/3 + string similarity ranks Neo high enough to pass. Frontend will populate the wrong device's specs. Fix idea in _pick_best_match: (a) require non-numeric variant tokens like Pro/Ultra/Plus/Neo/Lite to match verbatim if present in the query, or (b) apply a heavy penalty when the candidate contains a variant-token that the query does NOT contain (or vice-versa).

action_items: OPTIONAL/NICE-TO-HAVE: Improve _pick_best_match in /app/backend/routes/products_master_specs.py so that variant-suffix tokens (Pro / Ultra / Plus / Max / Neo / Lite / Mini) participate in the strict gate — currently POCO X6 Pro returns Poco X6 Neo. Suggested change: extend the `numeric_tokens` strict gate to also include a whitelist of well-known variant words, so a query containing 'pro' will only match candidates that also contain 'pro'. Add a regression case to the pytest for the fixed match.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/products_master_specs.py:291-340 — _pick_best_match handles numeric-token strictness but does not treat variant/suffix tokens (Pro, Ultra, Plus, Max, Neo, Lite, Mini, SE, FE) as decisive, which causes the POCO X6 Pro → Poco X6 Neo mismatch observed in testing. Consider adding a variant-token whitelist to the strict gate.

routes/products_master_specs.py:497 — the endpoint raises HTTPException(502) if spec_tabs is empty. Currently no test exercises this branch because we couldn't induce it against live GSMArena, so it is only theoretically covered.

routes/products_master_specs.py:472-485 — cache TTL check parses `at` as ISO string but silently swallows exceptions. If a cache row ever has an unexpected `at` type, the code falls through to a fresh scrape without logging — consider a log.debug so cache misses are diagnosable in prod.

routes/products_master_specs.py — file is 521 lines and self-contained (regex-based HTML parsing + brand list fetching + template mapping + endpoint). Below the 700-line hard limit; no split required, but consider extracting _TEMPLATE and _BRAND_URLS into a separate constants module for readability.
